messages:
support-jordan: FYI — customer Beth (acct: acme-ventures) reports intermittent 504s hitting the hosted /v1/generate endpoint during spikes. Saw spike around 12:03 UTC. They pasted curl + response. Can someone triage? :warning:

maya: Thanks Jordan. Any logs / sample request payloads? Is this affecting multiple regions or a single region?

support-jordan: Region: us-west-2. Sample obs from Beth: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxx' -d '{"model":"rw-medium","prompt":"hello"}'` 
Response: `504 Gateway Timeout` after ~60s. She says try again usually succeeds.

liam: I'll check infra metrics and K8s events. Initial glance at autoscaling metrics shows spike in queue_length metrics for the /generate route and concurrent requests jumped x6 at 12:02. KEDA ScaledObject for hosted-inference is configured on queue length.

liam: kubectl get hpa -n hosted inference-hpa: REPLICAS 2 -> 2, TARGET CPU 50%, current CPU 18%. But KEDA ScaledObject shows ScaleTrigger: queueLength with threshold 30, current 220. KEDA should scale. Running `kubectl describe scaledobject hosted-generate-scaledobj -n hosted` shows scale events but scale up stayed at 0 for ~30s due to cooldown?

paul-eng-runtime: Noted. Could be scale-up lag + model warmup. New pods come up but the model runner has a ~40-60s cold-start while it loads weights / warms KV cache. If gateway waits for readiness probe, requests will queue and hit API gateway timeout at 60s.

oncall-eve: I'm on it. I'm seeing recent change to readiness probe: httpsProbe path /ready now checks health of model process AND loads a small tokenized example which can block. That could delay readiness beyond KEDA cooldown and cause gateway timeouts.

sre-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: hosted-504-scaleup-lag-1776443210. Severity P2. Assigned: oncall-eve.

maya: Good find. Repro steps that I can run locally against staging? We should validate the readiness probe behavior and KEDA scaler config. Also need mitigation plan for prod asap (tenant getting timeouts).

paul-eng-runtime: Repro steps for load pattern that triggers: run 200 concurrent clients sending 1-2 token prompts with 0.1s interarrival until scale event. Example load script: 
```
heyload --concurrency 200 --rps 200 --url https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate --body '{"model":"rw-medium","prompt":"hello"}' --header 'Authorization: Bearer x'
```
You can observe `queue_length` metric spike in metrics/route.generate.queue_length.

liam: From k8s events: new pods started at 12:02:12 but readiness not passing until 12:03:05. Gateway timed out at 12:03:12. So warmup ~53s. KEDA scalableobject had scale cooldown 30s and stabilization windows of 60s, meaning autoscaler didn't apply expected replication fast enough.

support-jordan: Beth says the errors last for ~1min and then recover. She asked if they can get guaranteed availability during bursts because they're SLAd-eligible.

oncall-eve: Short-term mitigation options: 1) Increase gateway timeout to 120s for that route (risky), 2) Temporarily bump minReplicas to 4 for hosted-generate in us-west-2 to keep pre-warmed pods, 3) Add a pre-warm pool or warmup-container that runs model load in init container so readiness flips faster. I can apply option 2 for immediate relief. Thoughts?

maya: Option 2 seems quickest. Do we have capacity in the US-W region to add 2 reserved warm pods? Check quota and cost impact. Also add communication to Beth before action.

paul-eng-runtime: We should avoid changing the readiness probe to bypass model health checks — that would route traffic to cold pods. Better: make readiness pass early once process accepts RPCs but add a separate warmup metric for scheduling. Alternatively, change readiness to rely on a lightweight endpoint that returns ready after model loaded to a <20MB warm cache. Longer term: introduce pre-warmed pool and warm-attach for KEDA.

liam: I'll open a quick runbook change: bump hosted-generate minReplicas to 4 in us-west-2, and reduce KEDA cooldown (scale down stabilization) so subsequent bursts scale faster. Applying change now.

liam: `kubectl patch deployment hosted-generate -n hosted -p '{"spec":{"replicas":4}}'` -> OK. Monitoring...

sre-bot: ACTION: patched deployment hosted-generate replicas->4 in us-west-2.

paul-eng-runtime: Also adding a short-lived admission that we can use: pre-warm job to pull model into disk cache into container image layer? Might be heavy. Documenting follow-ups.

oncall-eve: After bump we see queue_length drop and 504 errors decrease. Beth confirmed reduced errors ~12:08. Will keep minReplicas change for 3 hours and then evaluate metrics.

support-jordan: Beth: "Thanks — much better now. We'll monitor tonight's spike window. Appreciate the fast response."

maya: Postmortem items: - investigation: KEDA cooldown + readiness probe blockers causing scale-up lag; - immediate mitigation: bumped minReplicas; - follow-ups: implement pre-warmed pool, adjust readiness to be non-blocking, tune KEDA thresholds per route, add synthetic traffic in chaos windows to validate.

paul-eng-runtime: Logging snippet from a starting pod showing warmup cost: 
```
[2026-03-10T12:02:15Z] model-loader: loading weights shard 3/8 (GPU0)
[2026-03-10T12:02:44Z] kv-cache: warming prefix cache size=1.2MB
[2026-03-10T12:02:55Z] readiness-check: model rpc ready=false
[2026-03-10T12:03:08Z] readiness-check: model rpc ready=true
```
Warmup ~53s matches observed gap.

liam: Action items assigned: liam -> create temporary runbook to bump minReplicas per-region for high-risk routes; paul -> design pre-warm pool and lighter readiness probe; maya -> postmortem + customer comms; oncall-eve -> monitor and rollback if capacity issues.

sre-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED: severity remains P2. SLA window recorded.

support-jordan: Customer asked if Dedicated or Reserved capacity would avoid this — explained that Dedicated gives predictable throughput and pre-warmed capacity, but we also need code paths for warmup. Beth asked for a short note about recommended deployment config for high burst workloads. Maya, can you send that?

maya: Will draft notes: recommend minReplicas >= expected concurrency / 10, enable pre-warm pool, set KEDA threshold conservative, and consider model quantization for faster warmup.

paul-eng-runtime: Longer-term engineering ticket: RW-INF-7623 "pre-warm pool + fast readiness for hosted inference". Estimate 2 sprints to prototype.

oncall-eve: Leaving monitoring on. Will close ticket when 12h of stable error rates.

customer-beth: Thanks team, appreciate the quick fix. We'll report if anything reappears tonight. :heart:

maya: Closing notes: keep thread for postmortem writeup. If anyone has additional logs paste here.
